description: Hello everyone! We are a team of passionate researchers and students from Thu Dau Mot University (TDMU) - Vietnam, specializing in Environmental Science, GIS, and Remote Sensing.  If you share a passion for Earth observation and want to build a meaningful project with us, join our team!
summary: The Climate Smart Farming Advisor is a free web tool built on Google Earth Engine that helps farmers and local agricultural offices adapt to hotter temperatures and irregular rainfall. Users simply click one point on the map, and the tool pulls NASA satellite and climate data for that exact location: SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG rainfall and drought frequency (SPI, SPEI), MODIS plant greenness, SRTM height and slope, and NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 future climate projections. It then answers three key questions: what to plant, when to plant, and which risks to prepare for, including drought, heat, heavy rain, and soil erosion. It also estimates a farm’s carbon footprint, so farmers can choose crops and practices that release fewer greenhouse gases. This matters because many farmers still rely on past experience and have few tools to assess current land conditions, and that experience is no longer enough under a changing climate. Our tool needs no installation, works anywhere on Earth, and is built on open, verifiable NASA data.
details:
What it does and how it works

The Climate Smart Farming Advisor is a free website. A user clicks one point on the map, and the tool retrieves NASA satellite and climate data for that exact location. It then turns the data into simple answers to three questions: What to plant? When to plant? Which risks should be prepared for (drought, heat, heavy rain, soil erosion)?

The analysis follows four steps:

- See the soil: SMAP soil moisture, plus SRTM height and slope, show the condition and terrain of the land.

- See the drought: GPM IMERG rainfall is used to calculate drought frequency with SPI and SPEI indices.

- See the future climate: NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 downscaled projections show how temperature and rainfall may change.

- Check the carbon footprint: The tool shows the greenhouse gases a farm releases as one number (CO₂ equivalent). MODIS plant greenness is also used to follow vegetation health.

Benefits and intended impact

- Farmers get a data-based guide instead of relying only on past experience, which is no longer enough under hotter temperatures and irregular rain.

- Farmers can see how often drought happens at their location and what the future may bring.

- Local agricultural offices can use the results to plan crops and water use.

- Farms can see their carbon footprint and choose crops and practices that release less, supporting a move towards green agriculture.

- The tool is free, needs no installation, and works anywhere on Earth, so even farmers with few resources can use it.

Tools, data:

Platform support: Google Earth Engine, with a web interface at https://nasa.rotoro.io.vn/

NASA data: SMAP, GPM IMERG, MODIS, SRTM, NEX-GDDP-CMIP6
